Most primary brain malignancies are gliomas, such as astrocytoma and glioblastoma multiforme. The frequency and natural histo- ry of brain tumours differ between children and adults. Low-grade astrocytomas, and medulloblastomas are the commonest primary brain tumours in children and ana- plastic astrocytomas and glioblastoma multiforme are the most common in adults. However, metastatic brain cancer is the most common cause of intracranial tumours in adults, being up to ten times more common than primary brain tumours. The cancers that most often metastasise to the brain are lung cancer, breast cancer, and melanoma. CNS involvement in patients with acute leukaemia (see Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia, p.651) or lymphoma (see Non-Hodgkin’s Lymphomas, p.656) is also quite common.
